rows.basis: Growth in gross 'Computer, network, machinery and equipment': 12,844M − 9,508M = 3,336M. This counts all server, network and machinery additions (net of disposals), not only AI, and predates Oracle's large AI build. It excludes buildings, land and construction in progress.

Growth in gross 'Computer, network, machinery and equipment': 17,258M − 12,844M = 4,414M. This counts all server and network growth, not only AI. It excludes construction in progress (+3,334M), which includes future datacenter shells.

Growth in gross 'Computer, network, machinery and equipment': 20,989M − 17,258M = 3,731M. This counts all server and network growth, not only AI. It excludes buildings, land and construction in progress.

Growth in gross 'Computer, network, machinery and equipment': 30,345M − 20,989M = 9,356M. This counts all server and network growth, not only AI. It excludes construction in progress (+10,876M) and buildings (+4,388M), and it misses finance-leased equipment (finance lease liability 2,934M at year end).

Growth in gross 'Computer, network, machinery and equipment': 59,634M − 30,345M = 29,289M. This counts all server and network growth, not only AI. The company says the whole 55,663M capex program supports AI Cloud Infrastructure, but that is a total-scope statement and is not used as the AI amount. Excluded are construction in progress (+23,463M), buildings (+10,382M) and finance leases (liability up 4,767M to 7,701M), so this likely understates the AI buildout.
The Q2 FY2026 earnings release says only that 'For years Oracle has been investing in AI and building autonomous cloud software.' No amount or share of operating expense is attributed to AI.
